scenes.vo: I'm Rifat, an IT contractor in Cambridge. In the UK, a tax rule called IR35 decides whether contractors are taxed like employees. When it changed, and the market slowed, my company stopped making sense. I had never closed a company before. So I treated it like any new skill: learn it with AI.

scenes.label: CHAPTER 1
scenes.title: The goal: transformation
scenes.broll: Goal infographic, three-step liquidation pipeline, legal debt separation
scenes.vo: Here's the real goal: transformation. Not just closing a company, but becoming someone who can learn anything quickly. Liquidation is my example: the legal way to close a company that can't pay its debts. The debt stays with the company, and a licensed insolvency practitioner, the professional who runs the process, sells the assets and pays creditors in order.

📘 Liquidation: closing a company that can't pay
⚖️ The debt stays with the company
🧑‍⚖️ The practitioner sells assets, pays creditors in order

scenes.label: CHAPTER 2
scenes.title: How I learned it: five steps with AI
scenes.broll: Numbered list 1 to 5 with live ChatGPT co-pilot interaction & learning animation
scenes.vo: Here's how I learned it, in five steps, with AI as my tutor, not my lawyer. This is what I learned, not financial advice. One: ask AI to explain the process in plain words, then ask it again, simpler. Two: check the facts against official sources, like HMRC, the UK tax office. Three: get a real expert. I chose an insolvency practitioner with 4.8 stars on Trustpilot. Four: turn what you learn into a checklist: stop trading, treat every creditor equally, bring every bank account to zero, or the money goes to the Crown, which means the government. Five: ask better questions every day, and act on the answers.

scenes.label: CHAPTER 3
scenes.title: What it cost and how long it took
scenes.broll: Cost and timeline graphic: £1,500 + £2,100, 2 months before + 2 months after
scenes.vo: What did it cost? For me, a £1,500 deposit, then a £2,100 balance to the liquidation company. That's the provider I found; yours may be cheaper or dearer, so plan for it. Getting ready took two months, and I expect two more after paying. The money matters less than the skill: you plus AI gives you leverage, and that skill carries into your next project.

scenes.label: CHAPTER 4
scenes.title: The honest part
scenes.broll: Exceptions cards, security guardrail badge, hands-on AI loop
scenes.vo: Now the honest part. AI didn't do this for me. When I stopped paying my accountant, I felt alone, and AI was where I turned. But AI is not hands-off: you stay hands-on, you check, correct and teach it. The practitioner is your safety net, so check what you give them. And some things stay personal: wrongful trading, personal guarantees, and money you owe from a director's loan.
overlay: ⚠️ AI didn't do it for me
🛠️ Stay hands-on: check, correct, teach
🛡️ The practitioner is your safety net
🚫 Some liability stays personal

scenes.label: CHAPTER 5
scenes.title: Three lessons from my inbox
scenes.broll: Online methods as database animation, MCP connection pipeline
scenes.vo: Three lessons from my inbox. One: nothing starts until the full fee is paid; my provider chased me six times. Two: keep everything in writing, online, because your emails become a searchable record. Three: connect your email and files to AI with MCP, a standard way to plug AI into your apps. When something goes wrong, learn from it and go again.
overlay: 📧 Three lessons from my inbox
1️⃣ Nothing starts until it's paid (chased 6 times)
2️⃣ Keep it in writing: a searchable record
3️⃣ MCP: a standard way to plug AI into apps

scenes.label: CHAPTER 6
scenes.title: Workflows plus AI
scenes.broll: n8n deterministic cron email vs AI probabilistic reply workflow diagram, Friend's advice vs honour card
scenes.vo: To keep track, I use n8n, a tool for building automatic workflows, plus AI agents, small programs that act for you. A workflow does the same thing every time, so it's predictable. AI can surprise you, so it needs checking. Build around both. A friend asked, why show your real work? Because sharing the real journey is how we all learn. That's the transformation.
overlay: ⚙️ n8n: a tool for automatic workflows
🤖 AI agents: programs that act for you
🔁 Workflows are predictable; AI needs checking
🏔️ Share the real journey

scenes.title: From shame to grace, and Part 2

scenes.vo: Closing a company can feel like failure. It isn't. Moving from shame to grace is the real breakthrough: a company is just a vehicle, and the skills you build stay with you. In Part 2, I'll show how I built the workflows and AI agents. Tell me in the comments if you want it, and subscribe to follow the journey.
